info.title: ALM Site Administration REST API Reference
info.description:
This guide provides a complete online reference for the Site Administration REST-based API. Use the REST API to access and work with ALM data in Site Administration. Consider the following when working with the REST-based API:
  • Ensure only authorized users can execute the automated script or job.
  • Do not include credentials as a part of the script or job.
  • Some responses might contain sensitive information. Ensure you store the received data in a secure way.
  • Limit access to data to authorized users.
  • Destroy output when the information is no longer needed.

Authenticate

To call any ALM Site Administration REST API request, you should first get authenticated to provide the authentication token as a cookie in the request header. We recommend you use the **alm-authenticate** or **login** methods to get authenticated.

Get authenticated by alm-authenticate with username

1. POST `/qcbin/authentication-point/alm-authenticate` to obtain an **LWSSO** token from `Set-Cookie`. For details, see [Non-Web Application Authentication](https://admhelp.microfocus.com/alm/api_refs/REST_core/Content/non-web-application-authen.html). 2. POST `/qcbin/rest/site-session` to open a site session by using the LWSSO token you obtained. This request returns `ALM_USER`, `QCSession`, and `XSRF-TOKEN` in `Set-Cookie`. For details, see [Session Management](https://admhelp.microfocus.com/alm/api_refs/REST_core/Content/REST_API_Core/General/Session_Management.html). 3. Wait for the cookies from the previous step to be returned before calling subsequent REST APIs. If you call subsequent APIs without waiting for the previous step, your application has multiple sessions open. Always pass the most recently returned cookies in the header of any requests.

Get authenticated by login with API key

1. Obtain your client ID and API key secret from your site administrator. For details about API keys, see [How to Manage API Keys](https://admhelp.microfocus.com/alm/en/latest/online_help/Content/api_keys_toc.htm). 2. POST `/qcbin/rest/oauth2/login`. This request returns `LWSSO_COOKIE_KEY`, `ALM_USER`, `QCSession`, and `XSRF-TOKEN` in `Set-Cookie`. For details, see [login](https://admhelp.microfocus.com/alm/api_refs/REST_core/Content/REST_API-shared/login.htm).

Headers

API headers are like an extra source of information for each API call you make. Their job is to represent the meta-data associated with an API request and response. Here are some of the most common API headers you encounter when using ALM SA REST API. Cookie Cookies are used to store small amounts of data. Except for the authenticate and session interfaces, you should set Cookie in all other interfaces to what you received from Set-Cookie. Pass Cookie for every other request in the request header. For example: Cookie: LWSSO_COOKIE_KEY={}; ALM_USER={}; QCSession={}; XSRF-TOKEN={}; Accept and Content-Type The `Accept` header is added to tell the server what types of response content your application accepts. You can refer to the `Media type` value of the response in the resource. The `Content-Type` header is added to tell the server what the media type is in the message body so that the server can parse the request body. It is usually required in PUT and POST requests. The value provided is usually `application/json` or `application/xml`. You can refer to the request body in every resource for details. X-XSRF-TOKEN ALM checks whether the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header is included in all requests, except the ones that use the GET HTTP method. If the header is missing, the REST API calls fail. After getting authenticated, the ALM server returns the value of `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. In all your subsequent requests, except for the ones that use the HTTP GET method, you should include the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header (that is the value of XSRF-TOKEN cookie) in the requests. More information can be found at [Send X-XSRF-TOKEN header with all requests](https://admhelp.microfocus.com/alm/api_refs/REST_core/Content/send_xsrf_header.htm?Highlight=site%20session#codeSample). customer-id This header is required only when you make REST API calls for SaaS customers and projects. It should be the ID of the relevant customer you are working with. Use the Get the permissions of the current user's role API to retrieve the correct customer id. After retrieving the correct customer id, set it in the request header in each API. If this value is not set, the default will be the customer-id you belong to.

SaaS Only tag

The SaaS Only tag is added to some REST APIs.This tag is added for the REST APIs that are available for ALM SaaS only. You cannot use them for on-premises environments.
For on-premises, all the APIs without this tag are available for use.

tags.name: Admin Report Resource
tags.description:
Provide GET and POST functions for admin reports.
An admin report contains the following project information: ping results, last login activities, active sessions, repository sizes, and database used space.
The ping results section contains information about how many projects (active/inactive/unavailable) failed to ping. This information is re-generated every 2 hours.
The login activities section contains information about user login activities in each project. This information is re-generated every 5 minutes.
The active sessions section contains information about how many active sessions there are in each project. This information is re-generated every 5 minutes.
The repository sizes section contains the information about the size of the repository: repository size and recyclable size (that is the physical files in the repository whose logical files were deleted so they can be cleaned by promoting the GC process manually). This information is re-generated every 2 hours.
The database used space section contains information about how much space is used for the DB server (SQL server/Oracle). This information is re-generated every 2 hours.

get.summary: Get audit logs
get.description:
Gets audit logs.

To avoid stress on the database server when there are a large number of audit logs, restrict the returned data by the query by filtering and retrieving only the required data.
You can indicate the total number of audit logs to return on each page using the page-size query parameter. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/audits?page-size=20
If a page size is not specified in the query, the number of returned entities on each page depends on the value of the REST_API_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE site parameter . If the site parameter is not defined, the page size is 100.
You can indicate the position of the first entity to retrieve using the start-index query parameter. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/audits?start-index=2
These two query parameters can be used together. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/audits?start-index=5&page-size=30

On success, the HTTP return value is 200 and returns the total counts of the audit logs and the full data of the audit logs in an XML/JSON string compliant with the AuditLogs schema.

get.description:
Gets all TDAdmin users in the project.

To avoid stress on the database server when there are a large number of results, restrict the size of data returned by the query by filtering and retrieving only the required data.
You can indicate the total number of project TDAdmin users to return on each page using the page-size query parameter. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/domains/{domainName}/projects/{projectName}/admin-users?page-size=20
If a page size is not specified in the query, the number of returned entities on each page depends on the value of the REST_API_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE site parameter. If the site parameter is not defined, the page size is 100.
You can indicate the position of the first entity to retrieve using the start-index query parameter. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/domains/{domainName}/projects/{projectName}/admin-users?start-index=2
You can also add extra fields you would like to include in the user details, For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/domains/{domainName}/projects/{projectName}/admin-users?extra-fields=group
These two query parameters and extra fields can be used together. For example: /qcbin/v2/sa/api/domains/{domainName}/projects/{projectName}/admin-users?start-index=1&page-size=30&extra-fields=group

On success, the HTTP return value is 200 and returns the total counts of the project TDAdmin users and the full data of the records in an XML/JSON string compliant with the Users schema.

post.description:
Realigns a repository.

When you create a backup of a project while the project is active, the time gap between the database and file system backups can cause discrepancies between the database file index and the physical files. If you restore the project from the backup, you must realign the file system and database tables.

To enable project realignment, set the SHOW_REALIGNMENT parameter to Y.

The realignment process performs the following actions:If a file is indexed in the database but is not located in the file system, the index of the file is removed from the database.
If a file is stored in the file system but is not indexed in the database, the file is deleted from the file system.
Verify the integrity of the relationship between the logical and physical database tables.

Projects are deactivated while the realignment is in progress, and activated again after the realignment is complete.

On success, the HTTP return value is 201.

Projects that are of version 11.5 or later.

To fix the problem, either reduce the column length to 4000 or add the columns to the alm_i18n_exceptions.xml exception file before converting. System-defined columns and system-defined user fields must be reduced and cannot be added to the exception file.
